concepts.title: Trial onboarding

claims.text: Effective May 1, 2026, enterprise trials require assisted onboarding. Smaller customers may continue with self-service trials.

evidence.quote: From May 1, 2026, enterprise trials require assisted onboarding. Smaller customers may continue with self-service trials.

claims.text: January 15: a 14-day self-service trial for every segment was proposed, but not approved.

evidence.quote: We propose offering a 14-day self-service trial to every customer segment.

claims.text: February 3: all-segment 14-day self-service trials were approved for a pilot ending April 30, 2026.

evidence.quote: Approved: run a 14-day self-service trial for all customer segments through April 30, 2026.

claims.text: April 24: assisted enterprise onboarding was recommended, not yet approved.

evidence.quote: This review recommends a change; it does not approve that change.
We recommend assisted onboarding for enterprise trials.

claims.text: The May decision followed configuration difficulties reported in April and replaced the pilot arrangement.

evidence.quote: This follows the setup difficulties described in the April pilot review and replaces the all-segment self-service arrangement used during the pilot.
Several larger customers needed help configuring their accounts during the pilot.

unknowns: These sources do not define enterprise or smaller customer, so an employee-count threshold cannot be inferred.
These sources do not establish who can approve an exception or whether exceptions are allowed.
The May decision does not establish the ongoing trial duration; 14 days was explicitly approved for the pilot.
These sources do not establish changes after May 1, 2026.
